svg.title: Allocate Capital Before Funding Advertising Expansion
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Capital Before Funding Advertising Expansion; subtitle: Four buckets across $30,000, $100,000, and $250,000 startup envelopes.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values encode the $100,000 planning stack in USD. Each stage also states its $30,000 and $250,000 comparison allocations. These are startup funding envelopes, not the Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual revenue scenarios.; caption: Lean: $12,000 + $6,000 + $4,000 + $8,000 = $30,000. Planning: $40,000 + $20,000 + $15,000 + $25,000 = $100,000. Expanded: $100,000 + $50,000 + $35,000 + $65,000 = $250,000.; stages: label: Opening inventory and supplier purchase commitments; value: Lean $12,000; planning $40,000; expanded $100,000; numeric value: 40000.0; detail: Fund landed inventory and supplier deposits with SKU-level sell-through limits. Keep purchase cash outflow separate from cost of goods recognized when products sell.; label: Acquisition testing and launch creative production; value: Lean $6,000; planning $20,000; expanded $50,000; numeric value: 20000.0; detail: Release spend in measured cohorts across creative, product pages, and paid traffic. Stop additional funding when retained-order contribution fails the underwriting target.; label: Storefront, integrations, and fulfillment onboarding setup; value: Lean $4,000; planning $15,000; expanded $35,000; numeric value: 15000.0; detail: Budget Shopify configuration, 3PL onboarding, product data, routing tests, and returns setup. Separate one-time implementation payments from recurring software and service expenses.; label: Operating liquidity and exception recovery reserve; value: Lean $8,000; planning $25,000; expanded $65,000; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Hold cash for settlement delays, replacements, refunds, and operating expenses. Against the canonical $4,000–$25,000 monthly opex range, the planning reserve alone covers approximately 1–6.25 months before replenishment cash needs.
